$comment: Every figure this project publishes as a measurement, with where it came from.
Why: the re-verification numbers appear in eight places across README, SECURITY, the tool
descriptions shipped in dist/, CLAUDE.md and two scripts. On 2026-08-26 a question from
csitte.at about one of them cost half an hour, because the figure was found in one bridge
thread while the measurement it came from was in another — and the first, wrong conclusion
was that our number was a typo. It was not; there were two measurements, and nothing next to
The same lookup also showed the figures had drifted apart in the repository itself: the
README table said 131 threads for `category:updates is:unread` while six other places said
132 for the same query, both dated 15.08. Two measurements, one date, no way to tell.
So: define each measurement once, here, and let a test check that what the prose says matches.
A figure that is not in this file is a figure nobody can trace back.

threads-list-drift-2026-08-15.what: Three raw-index queries through threads.list, each hit re-read for its true labels.
threads-list-drift-2026-08-15.source: session-bridge thread 110-gmail-index-reverify-messung, message 2026-08-15T213648Z from the gmail session — the full table, measured on request
threads-list-drift-2026-08-15.control: The same queries without `is:unread` return 800+ threads, so the predicate is applied rather than dropped.
threads-list-drift-2026-08-15.caution: csitte.at cites the SECOND row (128 hits / 14 with an unread message) because their page uses that query, with `-in:inbox`. Do not read their figures and ours as disagreeing: different query, and a night apart from the endpoint split below.

endpoint-split-2026-08-16.what: The same query through both endpoints, minutes apart, to locate where the drift sits.
endpoint-split-2026-08-16.source: session-bridge thread 061-mailwarden-doku-csitte-update, message 2026-08-16T071051Z — a follow-up measured that night because our own wording had jumped an endpoint boundary
endpoint-split-2026-08-16.caution: The threads.list figure here is 132, one more than the 131 measured the evening before for the same query — a message arrived in between. Both are correct for their moment. What this measurement is FOR is the endpoint contrast (132/114 against 19/0), not the absolute count; quote it with its own date, never as '15.08.'.

second-mailbox-2026-08-15.what: A second mailbox measured the same way on the same day, as a control.
second-mailbox-2026-08-15.source: session-bridge thread 110-gmail-index-reverify-messung, message 2026-08-15T211036Z from the gmail-csitte session
second-mailbox-2026-08-15.caution: Zero drift here is why the claim is 'a property of a mailbox', not of Gmail. It is not a counter-example to any cause: no thread in that mailbox was ever archived while still unread, which is the only shape a stale read-state can take.
